items.last: On the Postgres side, the table gets roughly 2M updates a day, mostly to the `status` column. Each update writes a new tuple version, and the old one becomes dead until vacuum reclaims it. The default autovacuum scale factor is 0.2, so it triggers after 20% of rows are dead, which for this table is about 8M rows. That sounds like a lot, but it keeps up because vacuum is cheap on a table this narrow. In short, autovacuum should handle it.

Here's the short version. The event loop runs one macrotask (a timer callback, an I/O callback, a message event), then drains the entire microtask queue (resolved promise callbacks, queueMicrotask) before rendering or picking the next macrotask. That's why your `Promise.resolve().then(...)` logs before the `setTimeout(..., 0)` even though the timeout was scheduled first, and why an infinite chain of microtasks can freeze the page.
